title: U.S. House · California's 15th Congressional District
area: San Mateo County on the San Francisco Peninsula, including South San Francisco, San Mateo, and East Palo Alto.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Kevin Mullin and Republican Charles Hoelter advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Anthony Dang, Mantosh Kumar, and Jim Garrity.

candidates.name: Kevin Mullin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 65% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 15th Congressional District (since 2023); previously California State Assembly (2012-2022)

summary.text: Kevin Mullin is the Democratic incumbent for California's 15th Congressional District on the San Francisco Peninsula. A San Mateo County native, he ran a small communications business, served on the South San Francisco City Council and as mayor, and spent a decade in the California State Assembly, where he was Speaker pro Tem. He was first elected to Congress in 2022 and serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee.

background.text: Born in San Mateo County, California; his official biography calls him a fourth-generation Californian and San Mateo County native, and says he is the son of a high school government teacher.

Graduated from Junipero Serra High School in San Mateo. Earned a bachelor's degree in communications from the University of San Francisco and a master's degree in public administration from San Francisco State University; his official biography also says he studied leadership at Harvard's Kennedy School of Government.

Worked as an aide to Jackie Speier when she was a state legislator, and was a local small communications business owner (founder of KM2 Communications) and television host and commentator, according to his official biography.
Served on the South San Francisco City Council from 2007 to 2012, including a term as mayor in 2011.

Represented San Mateo County in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022 and was Speaker pro Tem from 2014 until he left, which his office describes as the longest tenure in that role in the modern era.

According to his official biography, had more than 60 bills signed into law as an assemblymember, including the DISCLOSE Act and Social Media DISCLOSE Act on political advertising disclosure, and helped create a $3.7 billion climate resilience package.
While in the Assembly, helped secure record levels of state child-care funding and streamlined the process for obtaining a child-care license.
Won the November 2022 general election for California's 15th Congressional District over fellow Democrat David Canepa, 55.5% to 44.5%, and took office in January 2023.

In the 119th Congress, serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Energy; and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees. In the 118th Congress he served on the Natural Resources and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

His official biography says he is hard of hearing and wears hearing aids and has advocated for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community; he lives in the Bay Area with his wife Jessica and their twin sons.

priorities.text: Says addressing housing affordability and the production of new housing is one of his major priorities, citing his support for the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and his authorship of the Weatherization Resilience and Adaptation Program (WRAP) Act.
Says he is focused on reducing the cost of living, citing his introduction of the Poverty Line Act to update how the federal poverty line is calculated.
Says he is a member of the Medicare for All Caucus and a cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act of 2023.

positions.summary: Cosponsors the Medicare for All Act of 2023 and is a member of the Medicare for All Caucus; says the country must continue reducing prescription drug costs and cap the price of drugs like insulin.
Cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act, which would restore and protect access to abortion nationally, and the EACH Act to repeal the Hyde Amendment.
positions.quote: I unequivocally believe in a woman's right to choose and will continue fighting against policies that restrict access to reproductive health care.

positions.summary: Is a member of the Congressional Renters Caucus and co-led the Prevent Homelessness Act and Eviction Protection Act.
Supports strengthening the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and cosponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to expand affordable housing production.
Says he supports a progressive, equitable tax code that asks large corporations and the wealthiest 1% to pay their fair share while keeping costs down for working families.
Cosponsored the Child Care for Every Community Act, which would establish universal child care and early learning programs, and is advocating to fund childcare programs in Congress.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Natural Resources and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee) in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Introduced the Poverty Line Act and the Weatherization Resilience and Adaptation Program (WRAP) Act as some of his first bills in Congress.
Served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022 before his election to Congress.

candidates.name: Charles Hoelter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 18% of the vote.

summary.text: Charles Hoelter is a San Mateo-based Republican candidate for California's 15th Congressional District. A retired UPS supervisor, he describes his campaign priorities as including term limits, voter ID and apprenticeship programs in high schools. His campaign site describes him as a conservative advocate for "freedom, faith, and family," and he advanced from the June 2 primary in second place with 18.4% of the vote.

background.text: Graduated from Lincoln High School and earned a bachelor's degree from San Francisco State University in 1989.
Describes himself as a retired UPS supervisor who worked at the company for more than 25 years.
Says he lived in San Francisco for 27 years before moving to San Mateo County, where he has lived for 36 years; says he has been married 31 years and has three children.
According to his campaign website, he has spent years building relationships in the community and listening to working families, small business owners, veterans and law enforcement.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026, top-two primary with 18.4% of the vote (30,476 votes); his survey response lists the San Mateo Republican Party as an endorser.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists topic areas including energy independence, veterans, Second Amendment rights, education, public safety, border security, and the economy and inflation, though detailed position statements were not posted on the site as of the research date.
Lists his top three campaign messages as keeping men out of women's sports, term limits for politicians, and voter ID requirements for elections.
Says he is passionate about creating apprenticeship programs in high schools nationwide.

positions.summary: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, one of his three key campaign messages is the quoted line, which this guide reads as support for barring transgender girls and women from women's and girls' school sports.
positions.quote: Working on keeping men out of women sports

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, endorsed by the San Mateo County Republican Party. Campaign-site 'Our Plan for Change' text (third-person) gives general statements on border security, law enforcement and the right to bear arms; his dedicated issue pages contain no detail, so no stances beyond transgender sports are recorded.

statements.quote: Charles believes immigration should be legal, fair, and controlled. A secure border is a national security issue and must be treated as one
statements.context: On his campaign website (written in the third person)

statements.quote: Charles supports law enforcement and believes in policies that protect communities and hold criminals accountable.
statements.context: On his campaign website (written in the third person)

statements.quote: Charles will always defend the Constitution, including freedom of speech, religious liberty, and the right to bear arms.
